subject: AWS/GCP marketplace billing data fingerprint mismatch — evidence request and next steps
messages:
From: Marketplace Billing Operations <billing@marketplace.aws>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Marketplace statement flagged: 11/2026 - unmatched usage fingerprints

Rafael,

We're seeing a set of usage lines in the November statement for EdgeScale that do not match seller-submitted meterings. Attached is the merchant statement extract (marketplace_statement_nov.csv) and two sample usage IDs where the fingerprint (usage_id + timestamp) differs from the metering records we have on file. The mismatches affect payout for SKU: SKU-ML-HighThroughput and a handful of short-duration bursts.

Can you provide: 1) raw usage export for the account for 2026-11-01 — 2026-11-30 (CSV with timestamp in UTC and local timezone), 2) any internal ratecard/proration rules applied in November, and 3) confirmation whether EdgeScale submitted any corrected metering records after 11/30?

If you can get the CSV to us by EOD tomorrow we can triage for the Dec settlement window.

Thanks,
Marketplace Billing Operations
Amazon Web Services

Attachment: marketplace_statement_nov.csv (CSV, 42KB)

Subject: Re: Marketplace statement flagged: 11/2026 - unmatched usage fingerprints

Team — I pulled a preliminary internal snapshot and attached rdw_internal_usage_snapshot.csv. High-level findings:
- Two clusters of lines (usage_ids ending in ...A3 and ...F8) show a consistent 1-hour offset when compared to the marketplace timestamps. Looks like a timezone conversion at submission (UTC vs PST) for burst records around midnight PST.
- There is a small proration edge-case in our ratecard module: when a run spans the monthly boundary, we prorate by seconds; AWS aggregates by event and then normalizes, which can produce a 0.01–0.03 token difference that shows up as an unmatched fingerprint.
- No evidence of internal re-submits after 11/30 in our logs. EdgeScale customer portal shows a single submit per usage event.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Marketplace provides raw metering JSON for the top 20 mismatched usage_ids (so we can diff event-by-event).
2) We can generate a normalized export (convert all timestamps to UTC, include original event timestamp and derived billing_timestamp) and then run a fingerprint join.
3) If differences are purely timezone/proration noise, request a manual waiver for small token variance (< 0.05 units) and process an offset rather than a full dispute.

Attachment: rdw_internal_usage_snapshot.csv (CSV, 170KB)

Naomi
Revenue Operations Manager
Redwood Inference

We pushed a small correction on 2026-11-30 at 23:59:55 PST for a high-throughput run (this was a manual reclaim on our side) — I do not believe that correction reached the marketplace before the settlement snapshot.

EdgeScale view: they prefer to avoid a full credit memo if the delta can be addressed as a settlement offset. If you need us to sign anything to support a credit request we can do that — I've drafted a short confirmation (credit_request_draft.pdf) if useful.

If we can confirm the delta is < 0.1 units per affected line and tied to the noted timezone/proration cases, please advise next steps for an offset. If it's a larger mismatch we'll request a formal credit.

— Ana Herrera

Team / EdgeScale — thanks for the artifacts. Summary and action items:

Summary of root cause (per Naomi's diff + EdgeScale metering bundle):
- Primary cause: timestamp normalization mismatch (UTC/PST) for burst events near the daily boundary.
- Secondary cause: proration rounding differences between our per-second prorate and AWS aggregation. Net financial exposure: approximately $1,120 across 34 lines — under our internal manual-offset threshold of $5k.

Action items:
1) Naomi to produce a normalized export and a line-by-line diff (due 12/03, attached to HS-34729).
2) Marissa to open the settlement offset request with Marketplace (include credit_request_draft.pdf as seller confirmation).
3) Marketplace: if you can accept an offset for <$5k, please confirm and apply to the Dec 05 settlement. If Marketplace needs a formal credit memo, notify by EOD 12/03.
4) Rafael to update HubSpot HS-34729 and log the final disposition for the EdgeScale account.

Naomi / Marissa — please confirm when the offset request is submitted so I can mark the case closed in Billing Ops. EdgeScale — appreciate the quick confirmation and the draft — that'll expedite things.

Rafael
